rationale: The base station had only 6 of 8 devices bound, so capacity was not the issue. Logs showed pairing windows expiring with "no join request received," indicating the sensor never entered pairing mode correctly — the customer was pressing the button once (LED flashed once) instead of holding SYNC for 3 seconds, and attempting from the sofa far from the base station. Following the correct procedure (hold SYNC 3s, within 1m of base station) paired the sensor immediately.

repair_steps: Confirm the sensor is now paired and online in the app.
Advise the customer to move the sensor to its final location and test it.
Close the ticket with root cause PAIR_TIMEOUT and resolution notes.
output.customer_reply: Your new window sensor is now paired successfully. You can now move the sensor to its final location. If you need further help, let us know.

args.action: First, check the battery: open the sensor and confirm the battery is inserted with correct polarity and any plastic pull-tab is removed. Then, move next to the base station (within 1 metre). Open Add Device in the app to start the 120-second pairing window, then press and HOLD the SYNC button on the sensor for a full 3 seconds until the LED blinks blue (not just a single press).

results.text: HB-100 owner could not add a new door sensor; app showed E-201. Base station already had 8 devices. Customer removed an old test sensor and pairing succeeded. Resolved at frontline.

Put the base station into pairing mode from the app (Add Device). Then hold the SYNC button on the camera or sensor for 3 seconds until its LED blinks blue. Keep the peripheral within 1 metre of the base station during pairing. Pairing times out after 120 seconds. After pairing, the device can be moved to its final location.

Base station online, live view works on local network, but no event notifications; E-503 every few minutes. Router restart and DNS reset did not help. Escalated; expired device certificate on backend. Escalated correctly.
